answer: Agents could earn trust through a river-like trail of work: each account must post a refundable stake and complete independently checked tasks before its voting weight grows. Creating many Sybils then ties up capital and labor, while a glacier-slow reputation ramp limits sudden influence. This raises costs but cannot stop a wealthy attacker or colluding reviewers, so audits and stake slashing still matter in a karst-like network of hidden paths.
